newsitem.title: USA: Second New York police officer shot in 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: Second New York police officer shot in 24 hours.

text.p: A New York City police captain was shot in the back and seriously wounded by a sniper outside the Bronx precinct where he worked, police said on Saturday.
Capt. Steven Plavnick, 47, was in serious but stable condition after surgery to remove the bullet in his back.
The 4:20 a.m. EDT (0820 GMT) shooting came less than 10 hours after a police lieutenant was shot and killed by a violent career criminal during a wild shootout in Brooklyn.

Police said they had no suspects in the latest shooting but were looking into the possibility that the attack on Plavnick outside the Bronx precinct, may have been committed by someone seeking revenge.
The station house is the same precinct where another officer, Francis Livoti, was recently cleared in the choke-hold death of a young man.
"Certainly that is one area we are going to look into and something we are going to take very seriously," Police Commissioner Howard Safir said.

Livoti's acquittal on Oct. 7 followed an emotional three-week trial in which New York State Supreme Court Judge Gerald Sheindlin decided the prosecution had not proven beyond a reasonable doubt that Livoti was guilty of criminally negligent homicide in the death of 29-year-old Anthony Baez in December 1994.

The verdict was greeted by angry crowds protesting the judge's decision. Since then, the 46th Precinct has been the scene of several confrontations between protesters and officers wearing helmets and riot gear.
